name: Andrew Bailey

summary.text: Andrew Bailey has been Governor of the Bank of England since March 16, 2020, appointed for an eight-year term after serving as chief executive of the Financial Conduct Authority from July 2016 and earlier as Deputy Governor for Prudential Regulation and chief executive of the PRA; he joined the Bank in 1985. On September 28, 2022, on the recommendation of the Financial Policy Committee, the Bank announced temporary purchases of long-dated gilts, fully indemnified by HM Treasury, to counter dysfunction in the gilt market after the September 23 mini-budget triggered collateral calls on leveraged liability-driven investment funds. The Bank announced capacity of up to £65 billion, bought £19.3 billion by October 14, 2022 (£12.1 billion conventional and £7.2 billion index-linked), and sold the holdings by January 2023. On October 11, 2022 Bailey told pension funds they had three days to finish rebalancing.

facts.claim: Bailey's appointment as Governor was announced on December 20, 2019 and he took office on March 16, 2020 for a term running to March 15, 2028, succeeding Mark Carney.
facts.quote: Term of appointment: 16 March 2020 to 15 March 2028.

facts.claim: Before becoming Governor, Bailey was chief executive of the Financial Conduct Authority from July 1, 2016, and from April 1, 2013 Deputy Governor for Prudential Regulation and chief executive of the Prudential Regulation Authority; he joined the Bank of England in 1985 and served as Executive Director for Banking Services and Chief Cashier among other roles.
facts.quote: He served as Chief Executive Officer of the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) from 1 July 2016 until taking up the role of Governor.

sources.title: Andrew Bailey: Biography

facts.claim: On September 28, 2022 the Bank of England announced it would buy long-dated UK government bonds on whatever scale was necessary to restore orderly market conditions, on a temporary basis and fully indemnified by HM Treasury, after the Financial Policy Committee noted risks to UK financial stability from dysfunction in the gilt market and recommended action.
facts.quote: The FPC noted the risks to UK financial stability from dysfunction in the gilt market, and recommended that action be taken, welcoming the Bank's plans for temporary and targeted purchases at an urgent pace.

sources.title: Bank of England announces gilt market operation
Financial Policy Summary and Record of the Financial Policy Committee meeting, October 2022

facts.claim: The Bank initially announced auctions with capacity for up to £65 billion of purchases of conventional gilts of 20 years and over, expanded on October 11, 2022 to index-linked gilts, and concluded as planned on October 14, 2022; it bought £19.3 billion in total (£12.1 billion conventional and £7.2 billion index-linked) using a backstop pricing approach under which it bought only at relatively distressed prices.
facts.quote: The Bank bought £19.3 billion of gilts between 28 September and 14 October 2022, comprising £12.1 billion of conventional gilts and £7.2 billion of index-linked gilts.

sources.title: Financial stability buy/sell tools: a gilt market case study (Quarterly Bulletin 2023)
Asset Purchase Facility Quarterly Report - 2022 Q4

facts.claim: The Bank sold £13.9 billion of the £19.3 billion portfolio between November 29 and December 16, 2022 and had fully unwound the purchases by January 2023; Bailey has said the Bank made profits of around £3.8 billion on the intervention.
facts.quote: Between 29 November and 16 December 2022, £13.9 billion of the £19.3 billion portfolio was sold.

sources.title: Asset Purchase Facility Quarterly Report - 2022 Q4
Quantitative Tightening (report)

facts.claim: On October 11, 2022, speaking at an Institute of International Finance event in Washington, Bailey told pension funds and the firms managing them that they had three days to finish rebalancing their positions before the Bank's purchases ended, stressing that the operation was a financial stability measure, not monetary policy, and had to be temporary.
facts.quote: His message to the funds and the firms managing them was that they had three days left, and they had to get the work done.

sources.title: Bank of England's Bailey tells pension funds they have 3 days to rebalance

facts.claim: The Bank of England told lawmakers in October 2022 that a number of pension funds were hours from collapse when it decided to intervene in the long-dated gilt market; the Commons Work and Pensions Committee later reported on defined-benefit schemes' use of leveraged liability-driven investment.
facts.quote: The Bank of England told lawmakers that a number of pension funds were hours from collapse when it decided to intervene in the U.K. long-dated bond market.

openQuestions: Site claim that the Bank announced purchases of up to £65 billion between 28 September and 14 October 2022, bought about £19 billion, and postponed planned gilt sales while continuing to raise rates: the £65 billion capacity, dates and £19.3 billion total are supported by Bank of England records; the postponement of gilt sales is reflected in the Bank's September 29, 2022 market notice on Asset Purchase Facility gilt sales, which was listed but not read.

Site claim that Bailey 'directed' the emergency programme: the Bank's records show the operation was taken on the Financial Policy Committee's recommendation and announced by the Bank; Bailey publicly set its October 14 end date.
Site claims about mortgage rates rising from about 4.7% to 6.65% and about LDI managers BlackRock, Insight and L&G were not researched here.
The Treasury Committee's report text gives the unwind completion as January '2022', which appears to be a typo for 2023.
